title: The Phoenix Lights
hook: In 1997, thousands watched a huge V-shaped craft glide silently over Arizona.

beats.label: THE CASE
beats.line: A mile-wide V of lights drifted silently over the night sky of Phoenix.

beats.label: CLUE 1
beats.line: Thousands of witnesses across two states reported the same strange formation.

beats.label: CLUE 2
beats.line: Later that night, a separate row of lights hovered motionless above the city.

beats.label: CLUE 3
beats.line: The Air Force later said flares dropped by jets explained the second sighting.

beats.label: THEORY
beats.line: That explanation covers some sightings, but many witnesses still strongly disagree.

beats.label: THE TWIST
beats.line: The larger V-formation before the flares has still never been officially explained.

end.line: What do you think those Phoenix lights really were?

description: On 13 March 1997, thousands of witnesses across Arizona watched a huge V-shaped formation of lights cross the night sky. The military later explained a second set of lights as flares, but the first sighting remains unexplained.

facts.claim: On the night of 13 March 1997, thousands of people across Arizona and Nevada reported seeing a large V-shaped formation of lights moving silently across the sky.
A separate set of stationary lights was also seen hovering over Phoenix later that same night.
The US Air Force said the later stationary lights were flares dropped during a training exercise by A-10 aircraft from the Maryland Air National Guard.
That explanation is widely accepted for the later flare-like lights but is disputed by many witnesses who saw the earlier, larger V-shaped formation.
Then-Arizona Governor Fife Symington, who initially mocked the sightings, later said he too had seen an unexplained craft.
The earlier mass sighting of the V-shaped formation has never been officially explained.
